en.title: Boil water
en.description: Bring a kettle of water to a rolling boil. This will be used to make the dough.

en.title: Mix dough liquid and combine with flour
en.description: In a small bowl, combine the boiled water with 3 tablespoons of soy sauce and 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil. Make a well in the flour, pour in the liquid mixture, and stir until a shaggy dough forms.

en.title: Knead dough
en.description: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for about 5 minutes until smooth and elastic. The dough should be soft and pliable.

en.title: Let dough rest
en.description: Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and let it rest at room temperature for 20 minutes. This allows the gluten to relax, making it easier to roll out.

en.title: Grind spices
en.description: Using a mortar and pestle or a spice grinder, grind the coriander seeds and mustard seeds until they become a coarse powder. This releases their aroma.

en.title: Grate carrots and mix with spices and garlic
en.description: Peel and grate the carrots. Place them in a bowl, add the ground spices, and press the garlic cloves through a press into the mixture. Stir well to combine.

en.title: Add remaining soy sauce and fresh herbs
en.description: Add the remaining 2 tablespoons of soy sauce to the carrot mixture. Finely chop the fresh cilantro (or other fresh herbs) and stir it in. Mix until evenly distributed.

en.title: Heat sesame oil until smoking
en.description: Pour the sesame oil into a small pan and heat over high heat until it starts to shimmer and just begins to smoke. Be careful not to burn it.

en.title: Divide dough and roll into circles
en.description: Divide the rested dough into equal portions (about 4-6 pieces, depending on desired size). Also divide the filling into the same number of portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll each dough piece into a thin round disc, about 2-3 mm thick.

en.title: Fill and seal chebureki
en.description: Place a portion of filling on one half of each dough circle, leaving a 1 cm border. Moisten the edges with water, then fold the other half over the filling. Press the edges firmly to seal. Trim any uneven edges with a knife or pastry wheel for a neat shape.

en.title: Heat oil for frying
en.description: Pour enough vegetable oil into a deep skillet to reach about 1 cm depth. Heat over medium-high heat until the oil is hot and shimmering (about 170-180°C).

en.title: Fry chebureki until golden
en.description: Carefully place the chebureki into the hot oil, working in batches if needed. Fry for 2-3 minutes per side, until deep golden brown and crispy. Use a slotted spoon to turn them.

en.title: Drain on paper towels
en.description: Transfer the fried chebureki to a plate lined with paper towels. Let them sit for a minute to absorb excess oil before serving.
